title: Modernising our courtrooms: introducing the DAVE programme
authors: Mike Edgerton, Head of Video, Infrastructure and Workplace

content.text: Courts and tribunals in England and Wales, and non-devolved tribunals in Scotland, are changing. The way we present evidence and run hearings today looks very different to how it did a few years ago.

Evidence is often shared as video, images or audio. And in some cases, people join hearings remotely. Digital evidence is now common, remote participation is increasingly used, and expectations from court users continue to evolve.

At HMCTS, we are responding to these changes through the Digital Audio-Visual Evolution programme (DAVE). This is a long-term investment in the infrastructure that supports how justice is delivered, and in this first blog, I want to set out what DAVE is, why it matters, and how it is helping to build a modern justice system.
Why we are investing in courtroom technology

Many of our courtrooms rely on audio-visual equipment that has been in place for years. In some cases, that equipment is reaching the end of its life, making it more likely to fail or no longer meet modern requirements.

When systems fail, hearings can be disrupted, leading to delays and increased costs. This can be frustrating for everyone involved, including the public. It can also affect how clearly evidence is presented and understood in the courtroom.
At the same time, the nature of evidence has changed. Video footage, images and recordings are now routinely used, and our courtrooms need to be able to present this material clearly and reliably.
We have also seen a significant increase in remote and hybrid hearings. When used appropriately, these can improve access to justice, particularly for vulnerable users.
DAVE has been developed to respond to all of these changes and ensure that our courtrooms are fit for the future.
